items.title: An immersion of a syntomic scheme into a smooth scheme over the base is a regular immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that in a commutative triangle with a syntomic morphism into a smooth morphism over the same base, the immersion involved is a regular immersion (statement lines 5672-5684). The counted proof reduces the statement to a closed immersion, applies the fibrewise criterion for relative quasi-regular immersions to reduce to the fibres, and then checks the fibres pointwise, where the local ring of the fibre of the syntomic morphism is a local complete intersection over the residue field while the local ring of the fibre of the smooth morphism is regular, so the defining ideal is generated by a regular sequence (proof lines 5686-5717). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard flatness and local complete intersection statements.
